h: Inner Judgment and the Repair of Distorted Vision

p: "Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself
that is, that you place in your heart judges and officers
And it used the words "in all your gates,"
and this is as they said (Sanhedrin 86b)
א׳ יוֹשֵׁב עַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת
one sits at the entrance of the Temple Mount,
one sits at the entrance of the Courtyard,
and one sits in the Chamber of Hewn Stone.
And they correspond to the holiness of the three camps:
"at the entrance of the Temple Mount"
it appears in its plain sense
that it is outside the Temple Mount,
and it is the holiness of Yerushalayim,
that is, on the Temple Mount,
and it is the holiness of the Levite camp;
and "in the Chamber of Hewn Stone"
corresponds to the camp of the Shechinah,
for it was already open, with half of it in the sacred area,
so that there was no partition in between
and they correspond to the holiness of the three Avos
וְזֶהוּ הַפֵּירוּשׁ תִּתֶּן לְךָ בְּכָל שְׁעָרֶיךָ
And this is the meaning of "you shall appoint for yourself in all your gates":
that there shine forth for you in the heart
the holiness of the three courts,
which correspond to the holiness of the three Avos;
for wherever the number three is mentioned,
it alludes to the three Avos.
And this is what the Baal HaTurim said:
שֶׁחַיָּיב אָדָם לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
for a person is obligated to greet his teacher on the festival (Rosh Hashanah 16b).
And the intent of this juxtaposition
is that the mitzvah of appearing on the three festivals
הֵם גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגֶד ג׳ הָאָבוֹת
also corresponds to the three Avos
and this is the mitzvah of appearing:
that the holiness of the three Avos shine forth
And likewise the meaning of "judges and officers"
that you place for yourself in the heart
which is the holiness of the three Avos;
"they shall judge the people with righteous judgment."

p: "for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise
and perverts the words of the righteous."
'and perverts the words of the righteous'
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ה, כ)
And it is in the manner of what is said (Yeshayahu 5:20):
הוֹי הָאוֹמְרִים לָרַע טוֹב וְלַטּוֹב רָע
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil,
who put darkness for light and light for darkness";
for this is the power of the evil inclination:
and to mislead him in the two matters,
in thought, which is in the mind, and in deed.
In thought, which is in the mind
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר יְעַוֵּר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים
on this it says, "blinds the eyes of the wise,"
for wisdom is in the mind.
and this is the aspect of "light for darkness
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים יט, י)
in the manner of what is said (Tehillim 19:10):
And the essence of fear is that he sees
the Holy One, blessed be He,
stands over him and sees his deeds;
and this is the essence of light,
And this is what they said (Sotah 49a):
"Purity has taken away the taste and the scent."
"And he shall be imbued with the fear of Hashem";
and "taste" is the reasons of the Torah,
the aspect of the Oral Torah;
and "Malchus is the mouth, the Oral Torah,"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ה, ב)
And this is what it said, "blinds the eyes of the wise":
and he does not see the light,
and the darkness seems to him like light.
And this is what the Sifrei said:
that he declares the pure impure,
for he does not see the light;
as it says, "who put darkness for light."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר עַל כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
And afterward it said, regarding the power of deed:
"and perverts the words of the righteous";
this too is that he declares
עַל אָסוּר מוּתָּר וְעַל מוּתָּר אָסוּר
the forbidden permitted and the permitted forbidden;
and this corresponds to what is said in the pasuk:
"who call evil good and good evil."
דָּבָר אַחֵר כִּי הַשּׁוֹחַד יְעַוֵּר וְגוֹמֵר
he does not leave his world
until He directs him aright in his ruling;
he does not leave his world
until he knows what he is saying."
and the explanations of it are many;
and some emend it, and there are versions:
But according to this, in the first clause
one would also need to emend:
"until he rules erroneously in his ruling";
and such a version is not found in the books.
that it comes to teach us the depth of the matter:
it is not to his detriment but to his benefit,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה
for through this he will return in complete teshuvah
And this is what it said:
He will direct him aright in his ruling,
so that he return in teshuvah
if the inclination misled him in deed,
until he knows what he is saying"
that Hashem Yisbarach will shine knowledge into him,
and he will rectify through teshuvah.
And this is what is said at the beginning of the parshah:
"Judges and officers you shall appoint for yourself"
the three holinesses of the camp,
which correspond to the holiness of the three Avos.
וְאָז וְשָׁפְטוּ אֶת הָעָם מִשְׁפַּט צֶדֶק
And then "they shall judge the people with righteous judgment":
that is, even if, Heaven forbid,
and "for a bribe blinds" is fulfilled,
and he puts darkness for light and light for darkness
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא יְדֵי עוֹלָמוֹ
nevertheless he does not leave his world
until Hashem directs him aright in his ruling;
and likewise if, Heaven forbid, he corrupted
in the end knowledge will shine into him,
and he will know what he is saying.
And this is what it says:
"and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment."
